notes: מֵעִם → cometh from fuses as a two-preposition compound headed on the opening מִן (rules 23, 30); cometh is the construction-supplied linking verb of a prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49), since a bare is in its place says what the Hebrew says. The competing added reading is named in the unit note.

Who made: the supplied relative joins the anarthrous construct participle; rule 41's articleless-attributive sentence reaches the same result as rule 46 here, since the participle stands in apposition to Jehovah.
